title: Special Days at Home
bigQuestion: Why do families keep special days, and how can we ask a friend about theirs?

story.title: A Light for Every Month
story.kicker: Mia's class makes a big calendar and finds something surprising.
paragraphs: Mia's class makes a big calendar. It hangs on the wall. Each child adds a special day from home. They draw it in the right month.
Sam draws candles in December. His family keeps Hanukkah. Priya draws small clay lamps in the fall. Her family keeps Diwali. Omar draws a moon for Eid.

Mia draws a tree with lights for Christmas. Leo draws red lanterns for Lunar New Year. Jas draws a parade in April for Vaisakhi. Ben says his family has no holiday. They have a big pancake day on his birthday.
The class steps back. There are lights in many months! Their teacher smiles. "Every family has its own days," she says. "Each one matters to that family."
story.think: What is one day that is special in your home? What do you do that day?

lessons.title: Days That Matter
lessons.mainIdea: Families keep different special days, and each day matters to them.
reading: A holiday is a special day. Families do special things on it. They eat, sing and spend time together.
Different families keep different days. Some days come from a religion. A religion is what a group of people believe and do together.
Some families keep no religious days. They may have other special days, like birthdays. Every family's days are real to them.

words.d: a special day that a family or group keeps each year
what a group of people believe and do together, like prayer and holidays

look.title: A Picture in Words
look.text: Look at the big calendar on the wall. There are candles in December. There is a moon in spring. There is a lantern in winter. Each picture is a day that one family keeps.
look.prompt: Pick one picture. What might that family do on their day?

check.q: What is a holiday?
choices: A special day a family or group keeps each year
A day with no school work at all
check.why: A holiday is a special day kept each year.

check.q: Do all families keep the same special days?
choices: Yes, every family keeps the same days
check.why: Different families keep different days.

check.q: Ben's family keeps no religious holiday. What is true?
choices: His family's special days still matter
His family is doing something wrong
check.why: Some families keep no religious days. Their days are real to them.

lessons.title: Saying "Some Families"
lessons.mainIdea: We say "some families" or "Muslims celebrate" to speak fairly about each day.
reading: Words can be kind and true. We say "some families keep Diwali." We do not say "everyone keeps Diwali."
We name who keeps a day. "Muslims celebrate Eid." "Christians celebrate Christmas." "Jewish families light Hanukkah candles." This tells who, and it is fair to all.

words.d: to do happy, special things to mark a day

look.title: Two Ways to Say It
look.text: Kai says, "Everybody has a Christmas tree." Nia says, "Many Christian families put up a Christmas tree."
look.prompt: Which way fits more families? Why?

check.q: Which words are fair to all families?
check.why: "Some families" is true. Not every family keeps the same day.

check.q: Who celebrates Eid?
check.why: Muslims celebrate Eid.

check.q: What does celebrate mean?
choices: To do happy, special things to mark a day
check.why: Celebrate means to mark a day with happy, special things.

lessons.title: Christmas and Hanukkah
lessons.mainIdea: Christians keep Christmas and Jewish families keep Hanukkah, often in December.
reading: Christmas is on December 25 for many Christians. Christians believe Jesus was born on this day long ago. Many families give gifts and sing. Some put up a tree with lights.
Hanukkah is a Jewish holiday. It lasts eight nights. Families light a menorah. They add one more candle each night. Many eat potato pancakes called latkes.

words.d: a candle holder; at Hanukkah it holds candles for eight nights, plus one helper candle
the day many Christians remember the birth of Jesus

look.title: A Line Read at Christmas
look.text: For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord.
look.cite: The Bible, Luke 2:11, King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: Christians read these words at Christmas. Whose birth do they tell about?

check.q: How many nights does Hanukkah last?
check.why: Hanukkah lasts eight nights.

check.q: Which holiday do many Christians keep on December 25?
check.why: Many Christians keep Christmas on December 25.

check.q: What do Jewish families light at Hanukkah?
choices: A lantern for the new year
check.why: At Hanukkah, Jewish families light a menorah.

lessons.title: Diwali, Festival of Lights
lessons.mainIdea: Many Hindus, Sikhs and Jains keep Diwali with small lamps and bright colors.
reading: Diwali is a festival of lights. It comes in the fall. Many Hindus keep it. Many Sikhs and Jains mark it too.
Families light small clay lamps called diyas. They make bright patterns on the floor. They share sweets. Many Hindus say the lights show good winning over bad.

words.d: a fall festival of lights kept by many Hindus, Sikhs and Jains
a small clay lamp lit at Diwali

look.title: Lamps by the Door
look.text: Look at the front step. A row of tiny clay lamps glows. Each has a small flame. On the floor is a flower pattern in pink, yellow and blue powder.
look.prompt: Which holiday is this? What clues tell you?

check.q: What is a diya?
check.why: A diya is a small clay lamp lit at Diwali.

check.q: When does Diwali usually come?
check.why: Diwali comes in the fall.

check.q: Who keeps Diwali?
check.why: Many Hindus keep Diwali. Many Sikhs and Jains mark it too.

lessons.title: Eid al-Fitr
lessons.mainIdea: Muslims celebrate Eid al-Fitr at the end of Ramadan, a month of fasting.
reading: Ramadan is a special month for Muslims. Many grown-ups fast. They do not eat or drink from dawn to sunset. Each evening, families share a meal.
When Ramadan ends, Muslims celebrate Eid al-Fitr. Families pray together. They wear new or nice clothes. They visit, share food and give to people in need.

words.d: a month when many Muslims fast from dawn to sunset
to not eat or drink for a time

look.title: The Month of Ramadan
look.text: The Qur'an says that fasting is asked of believers in the month of Ramadan. It says God wants ease for people, not hardship.
look.cite: The Qur'an, Surah 2 (Al-Baqarah), verses 183-185, retold in plain words
look.prompt: What does this passage say Muslims do in Ramadan?

check.q: What do Muslims celebrate when Ramadan ends?
check.why: Eid al-Fitr comes at the end of Ramadan.

check.q: What does fast mean?
choices: To not eat or drink for a time
check.why: To fast means to not eat or drink for a time.

check.q: In Ramadan, when do many Muslims share a meal?
check.why: Many Muslims fast until sunset, then share a meal.

lessons.title: Lunar New Year and Vaisakhi
lessons.mainIdea: Many families mark a new year in winter or spring, like Lunar New Year and Vaisakhi.
reading: Lunar New Year starts with a new moon in winter. Many Chinese, Korean and Vietnamese families keep it. They clean the house. They eat a big meal. Children may get red envelopes with money.
Vaisakhi comes in April. It is a special day for Sikhs. Sikhs visit the gurdwara, their place of worship. Many join a parade with music and prayer songs.

words.d: a new year that starts with a new moon in winter
a spring day in April that is special for Sikhs

look.title: Special Days on Our Calendar
look.cite: Common calendar facts; some dates move each year
look.prompt: Which day comes first in the year? Which comes last?

check.q: What might a child get at Lunar New Year?
check.why: Many children get red envelopes at Lunar New Year.

check.q: Vaisakhi is a special day for which group?
check.why: Vaisakhi is special for Sikhs.

check.q: Lunar New Year starts with what?
check.why: Lunar New Year starts with a new moon.

lessons.title: Good Questions
lessons.mainIdea: We can ask a friend kindly about their special day and listen well.
reading: Your friend's day may be new to you. You can ask about it! Ask kind questions. "What do you do on your special day?"
Listen to the answer. Do not say a day is weird. Say "thank you for telling me." Your friend may not keep any holiday. That is okay too.

words.d: to treat people and what matters to them with care

look.title: At the Lunch Table
look.text: Omar says, "Tomorrow is Eid!" Lily does not know Eid. She could say, "That's weird." Or she could say, "Cool! What do you do on Eid?"
look.prompt: What should Lily say? Why is that kind?

check.q: Which question is kind?
choices: "What do you do on your special day?"
check.why: A kind question asks and listens.

check.q: What does respect mean?
choices: To treat people and what matters to them with care
check.why: Respect means treating people with care.

check.q: Your friend keeps no holiday. What do you do?
choices: Tell them they must pick one
check.why: Some families keep no holiday. That is okay.

lessons.title: Being Together
lessons.mainIdea: Most special days share lights, food, songs and being together.
reading: The days are different. But many share things. Many have lights. Many have good food. Many have songs or prayers.
Most of all, many special days bring people together. Families, friends and neighbors meet. They share and help each other.

words.d: something a family or group does the same way year after year

look.title: Same and Different
look.text: Hanukkah has candles. Diwali has clay lamps. Christmas has lights on a tree. Eid has a big family meal. Lunar New Year has a big family meal too.
look.prompt: What is the same about these days? What is different?

check.q: What do Hanukkah and Diwali both have?
check.why: Both use lights: candles and clay lamps.

check.q: What is a tradition?
choices: Something done the same way year after year
check.why: A tradition is done the same way year after year.

check.q: Eid and Lunar New Year both have what?
check.why: Both have a big family meal.

review.q: Which holiday has eight nights of candles?
review.why: Jewish families light candles for eight nights of Hanukkah.

review.q: Muslims celebrate Eid al-Fitr after which month?
review.why: Eid al-Fitr comes when Ramadan ends.

review.q: Which holiday has clay lamps called diyas?
Vaisakhi is a special day for whom?

review.why: We name who keeps a day. Muslims celebrate Eid.

review.q: A family keeps no religious holiday. What is true?
review.why: Every family's days are real to them.
